sections.h2: Where is the Wexford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 437 E. Division St. in Cadillac, on the second floor of the historic portion of the courthouse. The mailing address is P.O. Box 303, Cadillac, MI 49601, and the phone number is (231) 779-9455. Parking and the main entrance are at the back of the building.

From downtown Cadillac, the county's directions say to turn east on Harris Street and go four blocks, and the courthouse is on the north side of the street. Cadillac is the county seat and the largest city in Wexford County. The courthouse fight that put it there is part of county lore: the seat sat in Sherman, then Manton in 1881, and Cadillac won a county-wide vote in April 1882.

Documents may be mailed in with the recording fees and a self-addressed stamped envelope, since the office returns them by post. It must have the original document with original signatures, because state statute does not allow a copy to be recorded.

sections.h2: How much does the Wexford County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording costs $30.00 per document regardless of page count. The county notes that the figure includes the Michigan remonumentation fee and the Register of Deeds automation fee, and that it has applied statewide since October 1, 2016. The office takes cash, checks and credit cards, with checks payable to Register of Deeds.

  • Tax certification: $5.00, required on all warranty deeds and land contracts.
  • A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument: $3.00 for each instrument, on top of the $30.00.
  • Fixture filing: $30.00.
  • Copies: $1.00 per page. Certified document: $5.00.
  • Search fees: $5.00 per name, plus $0.50 per year searched. A UCC search is $6.00 per name, and a state, federal, MESC or judgment search is $3.00 per name.
  • Track index: $50 per hour or $25 per half hour.
  • Email convenience fee: $3.00.

Blank fill-in forms for quit claim deeds, warranty deeds, mineral deeds and non-construction liens are sold at the counter for $5.00. The office states plainly that it does not prepare legal documents or give legal advice and recommends an attorney for a deed.

sections.h2: What is the transfer tax on a Wexford County sale?
sections.html:
The county's printed tax table lists a state tax and a county tax for each price band of $500. One check payable to the Wexford County Register of Deeds can cover transfer tax, tax certification and recording fees together.

First rows of the Wexford County Register of Deeds transfer tax table, as printed by the county
Sale price bandStateCountyTotal
$100.01 to $500$3.75$0.55$4.30
$500.01 to $1,000$7.50$1.10$8.60
$1,000.01 to $1,500$11.25$1.65$12.90

The pattern in the table is the same in every band: $3.75 state and $0.55 county for each $500. The county's published table stops at $100,000, so for a typical house price ask the Register's staff to compute the exact amount before you bring a check. Exemptions come from MCL 207.505 (county tax) and MCL 207.526 (state tax) and have to be cited on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: Which requirements does a deed have to meet in Wexford County?
sections.html:
The county lists 17 requirements with statute citations. The ones sellers trip on most are practical, and the office checks each document against the list before recording it.

  • Signatures are original, with names typed or printed beneath them, and the names in the notary acknowledgment match those names.
  • The grantee's street or post office address appears in each deed or assignment.
  • The name and address of the person who drafted the document appear on any document executed in Michigan.
  • The document has a 2.5 inch unprinted margin at the top of page one and at least half an inch on all other sides, with black ink, at least 10 point type, white paper of at least 20 pound weight, and a size between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The first line of print names the recordable event the instrument evidences.
  • A deed that uses the word survivor needs a certified death certificate or proof of death recorded or referenced by liber and page.
  • Court orders are certified and sealed by the clerk.

Unplatted land adds two statements. A deed must say whether the right to make further land divisions under section 108 of the Land Division Act is conveyed, and it must carry the Michigan right to farm notice about nearby farm operations.

sections.h2: Can a Wexford County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Partly. The county accepts e-recording for all document types except court certified documents and documents that need tax certification. A warranty deed, a covenant deed, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract, a plat or a condominium document therefore has to go in on paper.

The county's e-recording rules state that documents are processed between 8:30 A.M. and 4:30 P.M. Monday through Friday, excluding county holidays, and that payment is by ACH under its vendor agreements. The office collects only the fees set by state and local statute, while vendors may add their own processing charges. It reserves the right to reject electronic submissions that break the Michigan Recording Act, and a submitter who violates the state standards loses the ability to file until further notice. It names four vendors on its list: CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm.

sections.h2: What should a Wexford County seller know about older records?
sections.html:
A cyber incident on November 5, 2024 left the office unable to recover a small portion of documents, under 5%, that were first recorded between August 14, 2024 and October 30, 2024. The county asks anyone who sent documents for recording in that window to contact the office to confirm whether theirs survived or needs to be recorded again. A seller who closed in that period should make that call before listing.

The county's land records search is hosted online through the county site, and the office states that its records reach back to 1864. Duplicate microfilm copies are kept in underground storage in Grand Rapids. Anyone can request a copy of a recorded deed or mortgage once it is public record, at $1.00 per page. The office faxes prepaid documents and does not email them.

The office also has a Fraud Notify service that monitors a name or business name for recordings that could affect the property. Ask the office how to sign up.

sections.h2: How does Michigan tax law touch a Wexford County deed?
sections.html:
A warranty deed cannot be recorded without proof that taxes for the prior five years are paid, per MCL 211.135, and the county treasurer's certification is the $5.00 line in the fee list. Taxes owed on a parcel therefore have to be cleared at or before closing.

The Register's FAQ also covers common family changes. When a spouse dies and both names were on the deed, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. You will not receive a new deed, since the office only records. When you pay off a mortgage, you receive a discharge from the lender, not a deed. The county warns that adding or removing a name on a deed has effects on divorce, borrowing, taxes and probate, and says to talk with an attorney before changing a deed. After a sale the buyer files a transfer notice with the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a.

sections.h2: What does the Wexford County housing base look like?
sections.html:
Wexford County is mostly forest. It lies in the Northern Lower Peninsula, and the Manistee National Forest covers much of it. Briar Hill, at 1,706 feet, is the highest point in the Lower Peninsula. The county was set up in 1840 as Kautawaubet County, renamed Wexford in 1843 and organized in 1869.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 34,445 residents on 564.93 square miles of land, with 16,924 housing units. The owner-occupied housing rate is 80.9%, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $170,400 (2020 to 2024). Median household income is $61,085, and the county issued 191 building permits in 2025. Rural parcels often involve land divisions and farm-neighbor notices, which is why the deed statements listed above matter here more than in a city lot sale.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Wexford County?
faqs.a: It costs $30.00 per document, including the Michigan remonumentation and Register of Deeds automation fees. A warranty deed adds a $5.00 tax certification, and a discharge or assignment covering several instruments adds $3.00 for each.

faqs.q: Can I record a warranty deed electronically in Wexford County?
faqs.a: No. Warranty deeds and land contracts need tax certification, so they go in on paper: the original with original signatures, delivered or mailed with fees and a stamped return envelope. Approved e-recording vendors can submit most other document types.

faqs.q: Does the Wexford County Register of Deeds give legal advice on my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not prepare legal documents or give advice. It sells blank fill-in forms for $5.00 and recommends an attorney for preparing a deed.

faqs.q: How do I find out who owns a Wexford County property?
faqs.a: Contact the County Equalization Department or the assessor for the city, township or village. They give the name on the tax roll, which may not be the owner, and you then search the Register's records with that name.

faqs.q: What happens to the deed when I pay off my Wexford County mortgage?
faqs.a: You do not get a new deed. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage for recording. Your deed is the one you received at purchase, and a recorded copy can be obtained at $1.00 per page.
